analysis: A successful 14m sample only raises the exploratory safe lower bound; it does not validate a 14m production cap.
The next coarse probe at 16m should retain the same +3m planned gap and strict scheduler contract.
If 16m fails credibly, the initial bracket becomes [14m,16m] and refinement can test ~15m.
If 16m passes, continue coarse ascent rather than prematurely refining.
Operating-cap replication should begin only after an upper failure region is characterized or a practical lower-bound stopping decision is made.
The later handoff-policy comparison should use the validated cap envelope rather than the exploratory maximum.
This sequencing minimizes confounding between runtime limit, wake gap, and parallelism.
Current probe remains active until timing close is captured.
